title: Idempotent consumers, dedup keys and Kafka exactly-once
summary: The inbox table, choosing a dedup key, broker-side dedup, natural idempotency, and what Kafka transactions really guarantee.

steps.title: The inbox: dedup in the same transaction
body: At-least-once means your handler **will** see repeats. An **idempotent consumer** records what it processed, in the
**same database transaction** as the side effect:
```sql
BEGIN;
INSERT INTO processed_messages (consumer, message_id, processed_at)
VALUES ('billing', 'm-42', now())
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;              -- 0 rows inserted → already processed: ROLLBACK and ack
INSERT INTO ledger (order_id, cents) VALUES ('o-7', 1299);
COMMIT;                              -- then ack the message
```text
deliver m-42 ─► BEGIN ─► insert key ─conflict─► rollback, ack (duplicate)
│ok
side effect ─► COMMIT ─► ack
crash here? nothing committed → the redelivery processes it cleanly
Why the same transaction: "check the table, then do the work, then insert the key" in separate steps leaves two
gaps. A crash after the work and before the insert reprocesses; two consumers that both check before either inserts
both process. The **unique key** (primary key on `consumer, message_id`) closes both.
Key it per consumer: `billing` and `loyalty` both handle `m-42`, each exactly once. Delete old rows on a schedule
longer than any redelivery or replay window you support.

steps.prompt: The checkout page posts `PayOrder` when the button is clicked. A double click sends two commands with **different** message ids for order `o-7`. The billing inbox dedups on message id. What happens, and what is the fix?
options: Both are charged; dedup on a business key as well (`charge:o-7`, or an idempotency key the client generates once per checkout)
Only one is charged, because the inbox sees the same order
The broker drops the second one
Both are charged; the fix is to ack faster
explain: A message id dedups **redeliveries** of one message. It cannot tell that two different messages mean the same
business action. That needs a business key: the order id for "charge this order once", or an idempotency key
created by the client once per user intent and carried through every retry.

steps.prompt: Is the effect naturally idempotent (safe to run twice), or does it need a dedup key?
items: `UPDATE stock SET qty = qty - 1 WHERE sku = 'A1'`
`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (order_id) DO UPDATE SET status = 'paid'`
Charge the card at the payment provider
Set the order status to `Shipped` only if it is `Paid`
Append a row to the ledger
explain: **Set, do not increment**: an absolute value or an upsert lands in the same state however often it runs. A guarded
state transition is idempotent too. Increments, appends and anything that leaves your database (cards, emails, HTTP
calls) need a key: an inbox row, or an idempotency key the external API honours.

steps.title: Broker-side dedup, and its limits
body: Some brokers drop duplicates for you, within limits:
| Mechanism | What it drops | Limit |
| Kafka idempotent producer (`EnableIdempotence = true`) | a producer's **retried** batch, per partition | one producer session; a restarted producer has a new id |
| Azure Service Bus duplicate detection | a send with a `MessageId` seen within the history window | enabled when the queue or topic is created; window 10 minutes by default, up to 7 days |
| Amazon SQS FIFO `MessageDeduplicationId` | a send with the same id within **5 minutes** | FIFO queues only; or content-based dedup (SHA-256 of the body) |
| RabbitMQ | nothing built in | dedup in the consumer |
All of these protect the **send** side. None of them knows that your consumer already charged the card before it
crashed. The inbox is still your job.

steps.prompt: Match each mechanism to the duplicates it removes.
pairs: Producer retries of the same batch into a partition
A resend with the same MessageId inside the history window
A resend with the same id within 5 minutes
Inbox table with a unique key
Redeliveries to your consumer, for as long as you keep the rows
Idempotency key sent to the payment API
A retried charge after a timeout
steps.explain: Each layer covers one hop. A senior review asks of every hop: "what happens when this is retried?"

steps.title: Kafka transactions: exactly-once inside Kafka
body: For **read from Kafka, process, write to Kafka** pipelines, Kafka can commit the output records **and** the input
offsets in one atomic transaction:
```csharp
var pc = new ProducerConfig { BootstrapServers = "kafka:9092", TransactionalId = "fraud-scorer-0", EnableIdempotence = true };
using var producer = new ProducerBuilder<string, string>(pc).Build();
producer.InitTransactions(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));    // fences an older instance with the same TransactionalId
var cc = new ConsumerConfig { BootstrapServers = "kafka:9092", GroupId = "fraud-scorer",
EnableAutoCommit = false, IsolationLevel = IsolationLevel.ReadCommitted };
// ... consumer.Subscribe("payments-requested");
var cr = consumer.Consume(ct);
producer.BeginTransaction();
try
producer.Produce("payments-scored", new Message<string, string> { Key = cr.Message.Key, Value = Score(cr.Message.Value) });
producer.SendOffsetsToTransaction(
new[] { new TopicPartitionOffset(cr.TopicPartition, cr.Offset + 1) },
consumer.ConsumerGroupMetadata, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
producer.CommitTransaction();
catch (KafkaException)
producer.AbortTransaction();   // then rewind the consumer to its committed offsets and retry
(Real code commits a transaction per batch, not per record.) Aborted records stay in the log with an abort marker;
consumers with `IsolationLevel.ReadCommitted` skip them, consumers left on the default `read_uncommitted` see them.
What "exactly-once" covers: Kafka in, Kafka out, read_committed downstream. It does **not** cover the database row
you wrote, the email you sent or the card you charged inside `Score`: those need the inbox and idempotency keys.

steps.prompt: Which of these does Kafka's exactly-once (transactions plus `read_committed` consumers) guarantee? Select all that apply.
options: The output records and the consumed input offsets are committed atomically: both or neither
Consumers with `IsolationLevel.ReadCommitted` never see records from aborted transactions
An HTTP call to the payment provider inside the handler runs exactly once
A consumer on the default isolation level never sees duplicates
A database row written by the handler is rolled back when the transaction aborts
explain: The guarantee stops at Kafka's edge. Anything outside the transaction (a database, an HTTP API) is still
at-least-once, and the default `read_uncommitted` consumer happily reads aborted records.

steps.prompt: Complete the read-process-write loop and the setting downstream consumers need.
code: producer.Produce("payments-scored", new Message<string, string> { Key = cr.Message.Key, Value = Score(cr.Message.Value) });
var downstream = new ConsumerConfig { GroupId = "ledger", IsolationLevel = IsolationLevel.__3__ };
explain: The offset sent is `cr.Offset + 1`: Kafka offsets you commit are always "the next record to read". Calling
`consumer.Commit` instead of `SendOffsetsToTransaction` would commit outside the transaction and break atomicity.

steps.title: Write the inbox
prompt: Write a class `Inbox` that makes a billing handler safe under at-least-once delivery. Everything one call does is a
single **transaction**: either all of it is recorded, or none of it.
- `string Handle(string consumer, string messageId, string orderId, int cents, bool failBeforeCommit = false)`
1. if `(consumer, messageId)` was processed before → `"duplicate message"` (nothing changes);
2. if `failBeforeCommit` → the transaction rolls back: record nothing, return `"rolled back"`;
3. record `(consumer, messageId)` as processed; then if this consumer already charged `orderId`
(a double click with a new message id) → `"already charged"`;
4. otherwise add `"{consumer} {orderId} {cents}"` to `Ledger`, remember the order as charged for this consumer,
- `List<string> Ledger` (get-only), `int ProcessedRows` (how many processed-message rows exist).
Keys are **per consumer**: `billing` and `loyalty` each process `m-1` once.
starter: public string Handle(string consumer, string messageId, string orderId, int cents, bool failBeforeCommit = false)
solution: readonly HashSet<(string Consumer, string MessageId)> processed = new();
readonly HashSet<(string Consumer, string OrderId)> charged = new();
public string Handle(string consumer, string messageId, string orderId, int cents, bool failBeforeCommit = false)
if (failBeforeCommit) return "rolled back";          // nothing was committed
processed.Add((consumer, messageId));                  // same transaction as the ledger row
hints: Two `HashSet<(string, string)>`: one for processed messages, one for charged orders, both keyed with the consumer.
Check the message first, then bail out on `failBeforeCommit` before changing anything.
`HashSet.Add` returns `false` when the key is already there: `if (!charged.Add((consumer, orderId))) return "already charged";`
template: Dojo.Eq("redelivery of the same message", "duplicate message", dojoIn.Handle("billing", "m-1", "o-7", 1299));
Dojo.Eq("double click: new message id, same order", "already charged", dojoIn.Handle("billing", "m-2", "o-7", 1299));
Dojo.Eq("the ledger has one charge", new List<string> { "billing o-7 1299" }, dojoIn.Ledger);
Dojo.Eq("crash before commit", "rolled back", dojoIn.Handle("billing", "m-3", "o-8", 500, failBeforeCommit: true));
Dojo.Eq("nothing kept from the rolled back attempt", 1, dojoIn.Ledger.Count);
Dojo.Eq("the redelivery after the crash is processed", "charged 500", dojoIn.Handle("billing", "m-3", "o-8", 500));
Dojo.Eq("another consumer has its own rows", "charged 1299", dojoIn.Handle("loyalty", "m-1", "o-7", 1299));
Dojo.Eq("processed rows: billing m-1, m-2, m-3 and loyalty m-1", 4, dojoIn.ProcessedRows);
Dojo.Eq("final ledger", new List<string> { "billing o-7 1299", "billing o-8 500", "loyalty o-7 1299" }, dojoIn.Ledger);
